value: Isolde was named by a visiting schoolmaster.
unit: Isolde was named by a visiting schoolmaster who lodged at her family's house on Pear Hill. She grew up in Brierley and became a close classmate and bosom friend of Nell Harcourt. She pledged eternal loyalty and affection to Nell, exchanging letters, tissue paper bookmarks, and secret signals between their homes. When Miss Pembroke visited her family home, Isolde was apprehensive after a chaotic bedroom encounter, but Nell successfully mediated with Miss Pembroke on her behalf, leading to Miss Pembroke presenting Isolde with a silver bangle bracelet. Isolde attended Brierley School under Miss Agnes Thorne, participating in recitations, dialogues, and field trips alongside her classmates Opal Pettigrew and Odette Pullen. Though her mother at times restricted her communication with Nell, Isolde maintained her deep affection for her friend.

unit: After living in an asylum in Marden, Nell was brought to Grey Shutters to reside with Thirza Abernethy and Obed Abernethy. Though initially expected to be sent away because the household wanted a boy, she won over her guardians and came to view Grey Shutters as her true home. She established a firm friendship with Isolde Pembroke, taking a solemn vow of lifelong companionship in the Pembroke garden. She attended Brierley School under the instruction of Miss Agnes Thorne, excelling academically while engaging in a fierce rivalry with classmate Hugh Carrow. Her time in Brierley was marked by energetic misadventures, including accidentally dying her red hair green after purchasing a dye from a travelling German merchant. Over time, she matured into an outstanding scholar, preparing diligently for entrance exams and pursuing a career in teaching while offering deep comfort and companionship to her guardians.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy traveled to Alder River Station
unit: Obed Abernethy traveled to Alder River Station expecting to collect an orphan boy sent from Nova Scotia by Mrs. Alexander Tranter to assist on his farm. Upon arriving, he discovered that a young girl, Nell Harcourt, had been sent instead due to a misunderstanding. Despite his deep discomfort and apprehension around unfamiliar women and girls, he took Nell home to Grey Shutters. Over time, Obed developed a profound bond with Nell, taking immense pride in her academic endeavors and acting as her gentle advocate and confidant. On one occasion, seeking to surprise Nell with a stylish dress made in the latest fashion with puffy sleeves, his intense shyness led to a flustered ordeal while shopping at an unfamiliar store, where he nervously bought a rake and twenty pounds of unwanted brown sugar before enlisting Mrs. Sowerby to secretly purchase and sew the dress.
